title: Northumberland County Council- FloodAI, using AI to detect flash floods
summary: Northumberland describes an alpha-stage flood-forecasting service for six catchments. No issued warning or avoided flood impact is reported.
account: Northumberland's FloodAI research project is developing forecasts for six flash-flood-prone catchments. At publication, the system was at alpha stage and approaching limited piloting. No issued warning or avoided flood impact is documented.
purpose: Develop forecasts for flash-flood-prone catchments that lack suitable warning coverage.

ratings.reason: Improved flood resilience is the aim, but no warning or changed flood outcome is reported.
The developing forecasting capability has no reported operational gain with a definable depth.

ai_role.statement: Machine-learning models combine environmental and hydrological data to support flash-flood forecasting. At publication, the service was at alpha stage. No warning, response, or avoided harm is attributed to operational use.

evidence.citation: Local Government Association, AI case-study bank. Council or project account published by LGA. Hosting and editorial curation do not establish independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Northumberland County Council- FloodAI, using AI to detect flash floods

produced_by: The project covers six catchments and combines university research with council, Arup, Isle Utilities, and Environment Agency participation.
Training sources include Met Office, Environment Agency, and hydrological-model data.
must_hold: The source does not establish which conditions are necessary to reproduce the reported benefit.

headline: Northumberland develops FloodAI for six flash-flood catchments

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The deployer's report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
